decisions: All approved topics and branches kept. Renamed: 'Digital Filters (FIR, IIR, DFT and FFT)' to 'Discrete Fourier Transform and Digital Filters' and 'Frequency-Domain Analysis (Bode, Nyquist, margins)' to 'Frequency-Domain Analysis' (STYLE: a parenthesis only disambiguates); 'Small-Signal Amplifiers' to 'Transistor Amplifiers' so output stages and power amplifiers fit.
Electrical Measurements and Instrumentation is a branch of Network Analysis (the draft's fallback): about 100 expected questions, too few for a topic.

Analytical Chemistry stays a topic (SuperGPQA analytical alone is 396 rows) and gains a third branch, Analytical Data Treatment (errors, significance tests, calibration). Qualitative salt analysis sits in Titrimetric and Gravimetric Analysis.

Factor Models and Performance Measurement is placed under Portfolio Theory and Risk Management after Mean-Variance Portfolio Theory, next to CAPM. Trading and Market Making then has two branches, one below STYLE's three; the alternative is the draft's placement inside the trading topic.

Chemistry has no gas-law, kinetic-theory, solid-state or nuclear branch. Those chemistry-source questions go to Thermodynamics (gas laws, real gases, kinetic theory, pure-substance phase diagrams, statistical thermodynamics), Quantum Mechanics (Bohr model, photoelectric effect, generic box, oscillator and hydrogen-atom problems, radioactivity) and Material Science (unit cells, packing, voids, defects). Expect roughly 500 of the ~6,000 chemistry questions to land there.

Chemistry vs Chemical Engineering: Chemistry owns textbook equilibrium (Kc, Kp, Le Chatelier, van 't Hoff), Raoult's law, colligative properties, partial molar quantities and catalysis mechanisms; ChemE owns bubble and dew calculations, activity-coefficient models, K-values, flash, process equilibrium conversion and catalytic reactor design.

Estimates: Chemistry 5,460 (Physical 2,410, Inorganic 1,210, Organic 1,360, Analytical 480). Organic comes out above inorganic because ChemBench (organic 429, inorganic 92) and SUPERChem are organic-heavy. Chemical Engineering 980, Circuits and Electronics 1,180, Signals, Systems and Control 990.

Existing nodes that duplicate new ones (owner to confirm the moves): EM Waveguides moves into Transmission Lines, Waveguides and Antennas (no second waveguide node was added; the branch then holds 12); EM Electronic Circuits > Transistor and Operational Amplifiers (est 4) retires into Analog Electronics; QM Molecular Rotation and Vibration Spectra retires into Chemistry's Rotational, Vibrational and Raman Spectroscopy (approved rule: molecular spectroscopy is Chemistry); Heat Transfer's Mass Transfer branch (3 nodes, 18 rows) moves to ChemE Diffusion and Mass Transfer Coefficients; FM Particle Settling and Separation and Fluidized and Packed Beds move to ChemE Settling, Filtration and Fluidisation (FM keeps single-body drag); MS Electron Configuration and the Periodic Table retires into Chemistry's Atomic Structure and Periodicity.

Notes to narrow: QF Expected Utility Maximization drops 'Kelly betting'; Statistics General Linear Model drops 'ridge penalty'; PSPE Diode Rectifiers keeps three-phase and converter rectifiers (single-phase rectifiers with capacitor filters are now in Analog Electronics); MS Electrochemical Cells and Electrode Potentials keeps corrosion cells only; MS Polymerization and Polymer Processing keeps processing (monomers and named polymers are Chemistry).

Statistics had neither Time Series Analysis nor Statistical Learning; both go under Mathematical Statistics, its only topic. Two subtopics are also added to the existing Linear Models branch (Regression Diagnostics, Generalized Linear Models; evidence: MMLU econometrics, SOA SRM). Their anchor after-branch 'Linear Models' means: append at the end of that branch. AR and MA autocovariances, linear prediction and spectral densities stay in Probability.

Resonance: plain series and parallel RLC resonance (Q, bandwidth) stays in EM's Resonance in AC Circuits; the C&E branch holds tank circuits with lossy coils and passive filters. Basic DC, transient and phasor circuits stay in EM; C&E nodes are named for dependent sources, Laplace methods and two-ports.

Placement calls: S-parameters in Two-Port Networks (not EM); optical fibre (SuperGPQA 50 rows) in the EM branch as a waveguide; magnetically coupled circuits in Two-Port Networks; molecular symmetry and point groups in Chemical Bonding; Latimer diagrams in Electrochemistry; stability constants in Coordination Chemistry (Ionic Equilibrium points there).

Open for the owner: game theory (auctions, Nash, bidding; QuantQA 34 rows) and Fermi estimation have no home; microprocessors, sampled-data control and SuperGPQA guidance and navigation (51 rows) are not covered; 'Named Reactions' is a recognised JEE unit but borders on a grab-bag.
